neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kısa adımlı yürüyüşüyle açıklanan örümcek kuşu adı merkezde yer alır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: الواقي الصرد (sihah;tahdhib)؛ الواق بكسر القاف بلا ياء (sihah)؛ قيل للصرد واق لأنه لا ينبسط في مشيه (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak anlatımı bu sözcüğü örümcek kuşunun adı olarak tanımlar ve son sesi bulunan biçimin yanında o sesin düştüğü kısa biçimi de kaydeder. Adın nedeni, kuşun yürürken adımlarını fazla açmaması olarak açıklanır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الواقي والواق اسما للصرد
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الواقي بمعنى الدافع ولا الفرس الواقي ولا السرج الواقي

root_profile.summary: Kökün merkezinde, zarar ile korunacak taraf arasına koruyucu bir unsur koyma fikri vardır; bu fikir kişinin kendisini korkulan veya yanlış davranıştan sakınmasına ve hayvanın ağrılı adımını gözeten bazı kullanımlara uzanır. Belirli ağırlık ölçüsü ile örümcek kuşu adı ise bu koruma çekirdeğinden ayrışmış adlandırma dallarıdır.

text.arabic_uthmani: لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَا طَعِمُوٓا۟ إِذَا مَا ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّءَامَنُوا۟ ثُمَّ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّأَحْسَنُوا۟ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

baseline.text: İnanıp iyi işler yapanlara, Allah'a karşı gelmekten sakındıkları, inandıkları ve iyi işler yaptıkları; sonra sakınmaya ve inanmaya devam ettikleri, ardından sakınıp iyilik yaptıkları sürece daha önce yiyip içtiklerinden dolayı bir günah yoktur. Allah iyilik yapanları sever.

findings.text: İman, onarıcı davranış ve tekrar eden sakınma, geçmişteki yeme eylemini giderek doğrultan koruyucu katmanlar oluşturur.

activation_trace.role: Negation denies a presently borne liability and supplies the release side of the mechanism.
Sinful inclination or constriction is the burden explicitly removed from the earlier intake.
Tasting and taking food supplies the retrospective act whose liability is being assessed.
Repeatedly placing the self in protection makes the condition an actively renewed safeguard.
Repeated heart-settling assent gives the protective sequence its inner commitment.
Purposeful action prevents faith from functioning as a merely named status.
Anti-corrupting action supplies concrete repair within the repeated trajectory.
Doing what is fine and beneficial is the sequence's culminating positive mode, beyond mere avoidance.

changed_reading.after: A retrospective release whose condition is an ongoing protective, faithful, reparative trajectory that culminates in ihsan.
changed_reading.before: A simple amnesty for something previously eaten.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction laysa ... junahun fima ta'imu removes blame concerning prior tasting, while the repeated idha/thumma sequence attaches that release to taqwa, faith, sound action, and ihsan.
baseline_models.mechanism: Current negation removes the burden of sinful deviation from the earlier intake, but the threefold self-protection, threefold trust, repeated purposeful repair, and final ihsan make the release trajectory-sensitive rather than a free-standing permission.

activation_trace.role: Provision, livelihood, and good condition widen tasting into lived benefit without detaching it from the focus verb.
The widened object remains governed by the explicit removal of sinful liability.
Purposeful conduct tests how received benefit is subsequently used.
Beneficent action turns received livelihood outward and supplies the endpoint of the broadened reading.

changed_reading.after: The clause can also assess benefits and modes of sustenance already lived through, by what the recipient subsequently becomes and does.
changed_reading.before: The clause concerns food already consumed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The object fima ta'imu is anchored in the focus root ط ع م, whose inventory includes livelihood and good condition as well as literal tasting.
baseline_models.mechanism: The tasted object can include what one has taken as sustenance, benefit, or lived provision. The no-blame clause can therefore concern a prior mode of life and benefit-reception, not only isolated mouthfuls, while the same ethical conditions govern the broader scope.

activation_trace.role: The focus act is bodily tasting, the material entry point whose moral mechanism the context differentiates.
Removed guilt must be distinguished from the context's retained account of harmful transgression.
Prohibition as prevention marks one boundary error: forbidding the good without warrant.
Release of a restriction supplies the lawful side of the consumption boundary.
Crossing a limit prevents lawful release from becoming indiscriminate license.
A drink that covers the intellect supplies the first causal link between intake and impaired agency.
Contaminating filth supplies the context's evaluation of the complex, not of ingestion as such.
Putting the complex aside supplies the required behavioral break in the protective trajectory.
Inner aversion opposite love identifies relational damage produced by the intake-linked system.
Turning people away from remembrance and prayer identifies its directional spiritual damage.

changed_reading.after: Blame is released from the bare past intake, while the mind-covering, boundary-crossing, relation-fracturing mechanism and post-warning participation remain morally decisive.
changed_reading.before: No blame attaches to past consumption when the eater is pious.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate context separates released, lawful intake from self-imposed prohibition and transgression, then identifies an intake-linked complex that covers the mind, contaminates conduct, generates enmity and aversion, and turns people away from remembrance. The focus release therefore does not make material consumption morally featureless; liability tracks the harmful mechanism and one's continued relation to it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies permission, prohibition, avoidance, and explicit social-spiritual effects. I infer that those effects explain why bare material intake and blame-bearing participation differ. A live alternative is that the context only identifies a categorical ban, without making causal harm the liability principle.
structural_cues: 5:87-88 pair lawful good consumption with taqwa; 5:90-92 then name a harmful complex, its effects, cessation, obedience, and caution before the focus release.

activation_trace.role: The focus's removed sin is the liability category differentiated by the oath mechanism.
Private tasting supplies the initial food relation that the context can redirect toward repair.
Being taken to account for fault supplies the explicit liability operation.
What is cast aside and not counted supplies the non-liable side of the intent distinction.
Deliberately binding an undertaking supplies the liable side and makes intention functionally relevant.
Covering or effacing fault supplies a reparative rather than merely punitive response.
Feeding another makes food itself a medium of restoration and reverses its direction from taking to giving.

changed_reading.after: Earlier intake is assessed through deliberate attachment and subsequent repair, with food capable of circulating from personal benefit into restitution for others.
changed_reading.before: The earlier eating is simply exempted.

context_deltas.mechanism: The oath passage distinguishes what is thrown away as uncounted speech from deliberately bound commitment, then answers liability with concrete repair, including feeding. This activates a culpability model for 5:93: past intake is not simply deleted from moral memory; responsibility depends on deliberate attachment and can be redirected through reparative action in which food moves from private consumption to provision for others.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an intent distinction and food-based expiation. I analogically carry that culpability-and-repair structure into the focus's no-blame formula. A live alternative is that oath liability and prior consumption are adjacent but legally independent topics.
structural_cues: 5:89 places non-accountability, deliberate binding, expiation, and two feeding expressions immediately before the intoxicant sequence and 5:93.

activation_trace.role: Prior tasting is the focus event whose place on the liability timeline is reconstructed.
Repeated self-protection supplies the post-disclosure disposition tested by later conduct.
A test that makes the inward condition appear turns later conduct into disclosed evidence.
Purposeful intent marks the breach that activates liability after the boundary is known.
Matching an act with its recompense supplies a proportionate repair mechanism.
Experiencing a thing as tasting mirrors the focus intake while reversing tasting into felt consequence.
Leaving punishment and effacing fault supplies the explicit treatment of the past.
What preceded fixes the pardoned act on the earlier side of the disclosed boundary.
Returning after withdrawal changes pardoned past action into culpable recurrence.
Dissolution of restriction shows that the boundary is categorized rather than universally attached to food.
Prohibition supplies the complementary category and its state-dependent limit.
Duration and continuance confine the prohibition to the time one remains in the named state.

changed_reading.after: Pre-boundary intake is not retroactively charged, but disclosure, intent, proportionate repair, and recurrence govern liability from that point onward.
changed_reading.before: Pious believers bear no blame for what they consumed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hunting sequence supplies an explicit temporal liability architecture: a test reveals disposition, deliberate breach triggers measured compensation and tasted consequence, what has passed is pardoned, recurrence changes the result, and the prohibition lasts only within a defined state. This sharply strengthens the focus as non-retroactive release rather than unconditional immunity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the entire past-versus-recurrence sequence and repeats tasting, food, and taqwa. I map that legal timing back to fima ta'imu in 5:93. A live alternative is that the hunting rules instantiate a separate regime and only illustrate, rather than define, the focus release.
structural_cues: The focus is followed by test, deliberate breach, equivalent repair, tasting consequence, pardon of what preceded, recurrence, and a duration-limited food rule.

activation_trace.role: Negation as exoneration blocks an unwarranted burden from attaching to prior intake.
Tasted food is the domain in which invented restrictions would otherwise produce retrospective guilt.
Demanding disclosure supplies a route by which avoidable burdens can be generated.
Pardon and effacement answer the urge to retroactively charge what was left undisclosed.
Denial that God made the named categories blocks their legal manufacture.
Fabricating a lie identifies the mechanism that falsely converts custom into prohibition.
Falsehood opposite truth marks the invented categories as invalid grounds for blame.
Claimed sufficiency makes inherited practice function as a closed substitute for guidance.
Paternal origin supplies the inherited channel through which the false food code persists.
Gentle direction to the true path supplies the valid alternative to inherited taboo.

changed_reading.after: No blame also protects prior intake from burdens manufactured by questioning, false attribution, or inherited taboo; taqwa is fidelity to real guidance, not maximal restriction.
changed_reading.before: No blame covers a past act under a newly stated rule.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later pericope warns that demand for further disclosure can generate distress, states pardon, denies that God instituted named animal restrictions, identifies their fabrication, and rejects inherited custom as sufficient guidance. This activates the no-blame clause as protection against after-the-fact or humanly manufactured food guilt: taqwa responds to disclosed guidance rather than multiplying taboos.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pardon, explicit denial of fabricated animal rules, and criticism of inherited sufficiency. I infer that 5:93's release also resists retroactive guilt generated by such rules. A live alternative is that the later material targets idolatrous attribution only, not over-prohibition generally.
structural_cues: 5:101-105 move from burden-generating questions and pardon to denied animal institutions, ancestral sufficiency, and responsibility under actual guidance.

activation_trace.role: Tasting anchors the bodily receipt that the table narrative turns into evidence.
Heart-settling security links the focus's repeated faith to the table eaters' sought reassurance.
A food-bearing table supplies the material platform on which ingestion becomes a sign event.
Eating the food makes verification bodily rather than merely propositional.
Settling and tranquility states the intended inward result of eating.
The heart is the locus where received food is meant to become settled conviction.
Fulfilled word and deed make the meal verify a promise rather than merely satisfy appetite.
Presence with observation converts recipients into witnesses responsible for what they encountered.
A visible sign makes the provision evidentiary and raises the stakes of its reception.
Allocated gift frames the meal as received provision calling for a response.
Covering a received blessing names the failed response after embodied evidence.
Afterness fixes rejection on the far side of receipt and verification.
Punitive pain supplies the intensified consequence of rejection after exceptional provision.

changed_reading.after: What is tasted can become embodied evidence and received provision; release from blame depends on carrying that receipt forward into truthful, protective, beneficent life.
changed_reading.before: What was tasted is a past material act from which blame is removed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The table sequence makes eating an epistemic and covenantal event: a supplied meal is sought so hearts may settle, truth may be verified, and eaters may become witnesses; the meal is also sign and provision, after which concealment or rejection intensifies liability. This changes the focus's tasting from morally inert ingestion into embodied receipt whose proper sequel is faith, protection, truthful action, and ihsan.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies eating, settled hearts, verified truth, witness, sign, provision, and post-receipt punishment. I infer that bodily receipt can deepen responsibility and that 5:93's repeated ethical sequel is how tasting is truthfully carried forward. A live alternative is that the table is principally communal feast and memorial, not an epistemic test.
structural_cues: 5:112 pairs taqwa with faith; 5:113 links eating to heart-settling, knowing truth, and witness; 5:114 calls the meal sign and provision; 5:115 marks rejection after receipt.

remaining_uncertainties: The scope of ta'imu may remain literal food consumption even though its branch inventory supports lived provision and experience.
The repeated taqwa-faith sequence may be chronological maturation, rhetorical intensification, or repeated facets of one condition.
The oath, hunting, invented-taboo, and table structures may illuminate 5:93 analogically without constituting one transferable legal rule.
strongest_changes: The hunting sequence turns the focus release into a precise non-retroactivity model governed by disclosure, intent, repair, and recurrence.
The immediate context relocates liability from bare intake to a mind-covering, boundary-crossing, socially divisive mechanism and continued participation in it.
The oath and table sequences make food move in two unexpected directions: outward as reparative feeding and inward as embodied evidence that raises post-receipt responsibility.
summary.what_was_special: Across four pericope movements, the packet repeatedly reuses intake, tasting, taqwa, faith, pardon, and consequence while changing their mechanism: consumption becomes a site of causal harm, calibrated liability, repair, protection from invented guilt, and truth-bearing reception.

activation_trace.role: Inclination toward a side supplies the spatial trace inside the focus's standard no-sin formula.
Repeated self-placement in protection functions as successive directional correction.
Moving a harmful complex to the side supplies a concrete counter-movement to wrongful inclination.
Being turned away from remembrance identifies the adverse direction that correction must reverse.
Gentle direction toward the path supplies the positive orientation of the repeated correction.

changed_reading.after: Secondarily, the intake need not become a lasting sideward tilt when each stage renews protection and redirects the person toward faith and ihsan.
changed_reading.before: There is no legal sin concerning the past intake.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the directional image of junah alongside its idiomatic guilt sense. It remains valid because the focus word itself anchors lateral inclination and nearby cues repeatedly encode putting aside, being turned away, and guidance. Render it only as a secondary spatial metaphor, never as a replacement for the legal meaning of sin.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Junah at word 7 can retain a trace of sideward inclination, while the repeated taqwa sequence can be heard as repeated reorientation.

activation_trace.role: Fruit reaching perceptible ripeness makes the earlier tasting a first maturation image.
A seed that grows and bears lets divine love function as generative fruition at the sequence's end.
Beneficent action is the ethical fruit produced by the repeated stages.
A garden enclosed by trees supplies the cultivated environment that activates the growth model.
Continuing provision and gift supplies the sustaining flow by which the ethical growth persists.
Stable endurance keeps maturation from being reduced to a momentary moral improvement.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they trace maturation: received fruit is followed by repeated cultivation until beneficence bears the enduring fruit of love.
changed_reading.before: The repetitions list legal-spiritual conditions for exemption.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain growth reading, surprising because it links distant seed, ripening, and garden branches to a juridical sentence. It remains anchored in the focus roots for tasting, love, and ihsan and is activated by the packet's final garden imagery. Render it as an exploratory model of ethical maturation, not as a claim that the words literally denote a cultivation cycle.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus moves from what was tasted through repeated protection and faith to ihsan and divine love; branch images allow tasting ripe fruit and love as a seed that bears.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Repeated caution progressively straightens prior intake.** `ج ن ح B003` is an offense as leaning away, `ط ع م B008` discernment/responsiveness, `و ق ي B002` protective caution, and `ح س ن B002` beneficent action. The threefold sequence advances from faith/work to excellence. I infer that exemption is not indifference to consumption but recognition of a repeatedly corrected trajectory away from crookedness.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Repeated guarding forms successive protective layers around past consumption.** Threefold fixed **و ق ي / B002** (“placing the self in protective caution”) alternates with belief, sound action, and beneficent action. 5:90–5:91 identified corrupt intake and its effects; 5:94–5:95 immediately stage a reachable temptation and measured response. I infer that repetition marks renewed guarding across changing knowledge and conduct, rather than a single retrospective label. The absence of blame reads as embedded in an ongoing protective trajectory.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:94 supplied the surprising prospective test: repeated guarding is verified not by retrospective claims but by restraint before prey already within reach.

words.gloss_range: defective negation opening a legal no-blame ruling
words.prose: {{ar:لَيْسَ}} ({{tr:laysa}}) opens by denying the very existence of blame in the ruling frame. As a defective verb, it makes the delayed blame noun the grammatically denied subject, while the burden phrase names who is being cleared. The protected group is heard first, then the negated liability arrives, so the ayah begins as exoneration rather than as mitigation.
words.root_gloss_range: absolute non-existence and negation; locally it negates blame as a legal predicate rather than merely reducing its severity

topics.headline: no-blame negation frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by removing blame as a legal reality, not by softening an existing charge.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as an uninflected negation verb with delayed subject, matching the CRITICAL rows about the laysa-plus-blame construction and legal exoneration.

words.gloss_range: preposition placing potential culpability as a burden on persons
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes culpability feel like something placed upon people. Because the phrase comes before the blame noun, the protected group stands in front of the reader before any liability is named.

topics.headline: burden marker for culpability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that blame is imagined as a burden on persons, and this burden is being removed from the described group.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the relative pronoun and marks the bearer of possible blame, preserving the CRITICAL burden image without turning it into a separate doctrine.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun defining the exonerated group by a following action-profile
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) turns the ruling toward a described class rather than an unnamed crowd. The group is defined by belief and restorative action, so legal clearance is tied to a behavioral profile. This relative clause is the first qualifying panel before the ayah moves to consumption scope and then to the staged conditions.

topics.headline: relative clause as group definition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exonerated people are identified by their enacted profile, not by a bare social label.
topics.reason: QAC places the relative pronoun under the preceding preposition and the following clause supplies the class-defining actions.

words.gloss_range: completed Form IV trust-belief marking the opening class and starting a repeated trust refrain
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) names belief as a completed marker of the opening class while still carrying the security-and-trust pressure of the root. Its later repetitions make trust a refrain, and its disappearance in the final stage lets excellence take over the summit. The supplied comparison with 5:54 supports the same trust-language field without changing the local sequence.
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, believing, and becoming safe; locally Form IV selects enacted belief/trust while retaining security pressure

topics.headline: completed trust as opening marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief begins as a completed class marker, then becomes a staged refrain before yielding to excellence.
topics.reason: The local Form IV perfect supports enacted belief/trust; broader security imagery survives as pressure, while repetition and disappearance are anchored in the ayah itself.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction binding belief and action without staging delay
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates trust with action as one opening profile. It does not make action an afterthought or later step; the two qualifiers stand together before the no-blame ruling is specified.

topics.headline: trust and action paired
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief and action are presented as mutually load-bearing parts of the described class.
topics.reason: The connector functions as ordinary coordination here, not as the staged delay later marked by thumma.

words.gloss_range: completed purposeful work taking the recognized restorative deed-class as object
words.prose: {{ar:عَمِلُوا۟}} ({{tr:ʿamilū}}) gives the opening class an acted profile, not only an inner trust claim. The verb is completed by the following restorative deed-class, and its later repetition inside Stage 1 turns the opening identity into a condition before action-language drops out. The same-surah comparison with 5:9 reinforces accountability around action without replacing the local object relation.
words.root_gloss_range: work, making, doing, and result-producing action; locally the verb selects purposeful action completed by its object

topics.headline: action completed by repair-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pairs trust with concrete restorative work before later compressing the sequence.
topics.reason: QAC treats the verb as transitive with the following object; the CRITICAL rows about work, paired construction, and later disappearance are supported by the local repetitions.

words.gloss_range: definite plural restorative acts, the recognized class of deeds that repair what is unsound
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ}} ({{tr:aṣ-ṣāliḥāti}}) makes the object of action a recognized class of restorative deeds. The feminine plural deed-shape packages enacted repairs rather than naming righteous agents, and the repair-root keeps the phrase from becoming a vague “good deeds” label. Its exact repetition in Stage 1 prepares the later move from repair to excellence.
words.root_gloss_range: soundness, repair, reconciliation, and being fit; locally the plural object names restorative deed-types

topics.headline: definite restorative deed-class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deeds are framed as a known class of repair, which later becomes the floor beneath excellence.
topics.reason: The definite feminine plural object is locally governed by the action verb; broad repair/corruption senses are kept as semantic pressure rather than as separate senses.

words.gloss_range: indefinite delayed blame noun, a culpable deviation denied by the opening negation
words.prose: {{ar:جُنَاحٌۭ}} ({{tr:junāḥun}}) is the delayed noun whose existence the opening negation denies. Its root image of leaning or wing-tilt makes legal blame feel like a deviation, and the indefinite form leaves no particular culpable tilt sitting on the described group.
words.root_gloss_range: inclining, wing-tilting, and deviating; locally the legal noun names blame or culpability while preserving the deviation image

topics.headline: delayed blame noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruling removes culpable deviation itself, not merely a named penalty.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the noun as the subject of laysa; the legal no-blame sense is selected, with the wing-tilt root retained as local imagery.

words.gloss_range: fused preposition and open relative marking the broad domain of exoneration
words.prose: {{ar:فِيمَا}} ({{tr:fīmā}}) opens the scope of the ruling as broadly as “in whatever” they consumed. That breadth is real, but it is immediately held inside the conditional frame that follows, so open scope and ethical restriction work together.

topics.headline: broad domain before restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consumed matter is deliberately left open before the conditions narrow the ruling ethically.
topics.reason: QAC parses the surface as fī plus mā; the rows correctly tie that form to broad scope and later conditional qualification.

words.gloss_range: objectless completed consuming or tasting, broad enough for eating, drinking, or palate-based intake
words.prose: {{ar:طَعِمُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:ṭaʿimū}}) keeps the consumed object unstated after the broad scope marker. The root’s tasting field makes the act concrete at the palate while remaining broad enough for drinking as well as eating, as the cited water scene in 2:249 confirms. In context after 5:90-91, this objectless verb lets the ruling address remembered consumption without narrowing it to one item.
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, eating, drinking, feeding, and sensory experience; locally Form I selects direct consumption without a specified object

topics.headline: objectless tasting-consumption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah clears a broad field of past consumption while refusing to name or narrow the object.
topics.reason: The local verb is Form I and intransitive in QAC; V4 and the cited 2:249 water use support broad tasting/consumption without making every branch equally active.

words.gloss_range: conditional time particle introducing the ethical qualifications for the no-blame ruling
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) pivots from the broad consumption field into conditions that qualify the no-blame ruling as a whole. Its expected-occurrence force makes the ruling read as “whenever this ethical profile is realized,” presenting the stages as attainable states rather than as a loose topic shift.

topics.headline: expected condition opens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broad exoneration is governed by an ethical condition rather than left unqualified.
topics.reason: QAC treats the word as a time or conditional particle; the following sequence confirms that it qualifies the ruling as a whole.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle after the conditional, strengthening the whenever-frame without adding an object
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is not the earlier open relative repeated in the same role. Here it intensifies the conditional frame, so the ayah moves from “whatever they consumed” to “whenever indeed they guarded themselves.”

topics.headline: same surface, new function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same short surface re-parsed from broad scope into strengthened condition.
topics.reason: QAC marks this mā as emphatic rather than relative or negative, preserving the CRITICAL contrast with the earlier fused fīmā.

words.gloss_range: first completed Form VIII self-guarding, beginning the invariant ethical refrain
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّقَوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqaw}}) begins the threefold refrain of self-guarding as a completed condition, not a future aspiration. The physical shield image remains under the ethical sense, and Form VIII makes the guarding reflexive: the group actively takes protective responsibility. The cited 5:2 pairing supports the ethical field, while the local ayah makes this verb the constant across all three stages.
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, shielding, preserving, and protection; locally Form VIII selects reflexive self-guarding

topics.headline: first shield-refrain verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entire conditional ladder is held together by repeated self-guarding.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form VIII perfect; the shield image and 5:2 ethical pairing are valid supports, but the local payoff is the threefold refrain.

words.gloss_range: assimilated conjunction pairing first-stage self-guarding with trust
words.prose: {{ar:وَّ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps self-guarding and trust inside the same first stage. The assimilated surface makes the join tight, while the grammar remains simple coordination rather than the later stage-separating thumma.

topics.headline: first-stage coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Stage 1 holds guarding and trust together before adding action.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the next perfect verb with ittaqaw, and the CRITICAL sound rows fit the tight local attachment.

words.gloss_range: second Form IV trust-belief, reactivated inside Stage 1 between guarding and action
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) repeats the trust verb inside Stage 1, so the opening identity becomes an explicit condition. It stands between self-guarding and action, making trust part of the fullest three-member tier rather than a label left behind at the start.
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, and belief; locally the repeated perfect activates trust within the conditional sequence

topics.headline: trust re-entering the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief is not only the opening description; it is reactivated as part of the first conditional tier.
topics.reason: The repeated Form IV perfect has the same subject chain as the opening relative clause and joins the Stage 1 triad.

words.gloss_range: second coordinating conjunction completing the first-stage triad
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the action phrase as a third equal beat in Stage 1. It prevents the condition from collapsing into inward trust alone by binding work to guarding and belief.

topics.headline: third member added
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Stage 1 is a three-member structure: guarding, trust, and action.
topics.reason: The connector functions as coordination within Stage 1, matching the CRITICAL triad rows.

words.gloss_range: second purposeful action verb, last finite work-language before the sequence compresses
words.prose: {{ar:عَمِلُوا۟}} ({{tr:ʿamilū}}) repeats purposeful action within Stage 1 and again points forward to the restorative object. This is the last occurrence of explicit work-language, so the ayah establishes the repair baseline before later compressing it into trust and then excellence.
words.root_gloss_range: purposeful work and result-producing action; locally the verb again requires the restorative object that follows

topics.headline: action before compression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices where explicit action-language reaches its final appearance before being absorbed into the final excellence verb.
topics.reason: QAC keeps the verb tied to the following object; the local sequence supports the CRITICAL claim that action appears in Stage 1 only before yielding to iḥsān.

words.gloss_range: second definite restorative deed-class, closing the duplicated belief-action construction
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ}} ({{tr:aṣ-ṣāliḥāti}}) closes the repeated belief-and-action construction by naming the repair-class a second time. Its disappearance after Stage 1 makes repair the floor of the sequence, not the final word on the ethical arc.
words.root_gloss_range: repair, soundness, and fitness; locally the repeated plural object names the same restorative class before it disappears

topics.headline: second repair-class baseline
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that restorative deeds are repeated exactly before the ayah moves beyond explicit repair-language.
topics.reason: The second definite plural object repeats the earlier form and sets up the later shift to the ḥ-s-n field; repair remains local, not opposed to excellence.

words.gloss_range: first sequence marker creating a delayed move from full triad to reduced pair
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) marks a new stage rather than simple addition. Its delay gives the ethical movement room to develop: the full three-member tier is followed by a reduced pair.

topics.headline: delayed movement to Stage 2
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is building stages of growth, not piling terms in a flat list.
topics.reason: QAC and the sequence both support thumma as a stage-separating conjunction with temporal or developmental distance.

words.gloss_range: second Form VIII self-guarding, carrying the same subject into a compressed second stage
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّقَوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqaw}}) carries the same group into Stage 2 with the shield verb unchanged. Because explicit action is no longer named here, self-guarding feels more internalized while still paired with trust.
words.root_gloss_range: guarding and shielding; locally the same reflexive form recurs with fewer named co-conditions

topics.headline: same shield in reduced pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guarding remains constant even as the surrounding conditions compress.
topics.reason: The same Form VIII perfect and pro-drop subject support continuity; the narrowing is that the local word itself signals guarding, while the internalization payoff comes from its Stage 2 placement.

words.gloss_range: assimilated conjunction binding the reduced second-stage pair
words.prose: {{ar:وَّ}} ({{tr:wa}}) gives Stage 2 a simpler two-member rhythm. It binds self-guarding to trust without adding the action-and-repair phrase that belonged to Stage 1.

topics.headline: reduced pair connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second stage as a compressed pair rather than a repeat of the full triad.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the Stage 2 trust verb with the repeated guarding verb; the assimilated form supports the close join.

words.gloss_range: third and final Form IV trust-belief before the sequence turns to excellence
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) completes the explicit trust triad. It still carries trust after renewed self-guarding, but its position is also farewell: the next stage will keep guarding and replace trust-language with excellence.
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, and belief; locally the final occurrence completes the trust chain before it disappears

topics.headline: trust chain closes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the last explicit belief verb just before the ayah changes its ethical vocabulary.
topics.reason: The third identical Form IV perfect is locally present in Stage 2 and absent from Stage 3, confirming the CRITICAL disappearance payoff.

words.gloss_range: second sequence marker opening the final developmental tier
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) opens the final tier with the same stage-marker heard earlier. The repeated separator makes the ayah’s three-phase architecture audible before the summit pair appears.

topics.headline: second delayed stage marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the last transition as a genuine new tier, not merely another coordinated phrase.
topics.reason: The second thumma repeats the first separator and introduces the final Stage 3 pair.

words.gloss_range: third Form VIII self-guarding, completing the invariant refrain at the summit
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّقَوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqaw}}) completes the threefold self-guarding refrain. At the summit it no longer stands with explicit belief or repair-work, but with beauty-making, so restraint remains present inside excellence rather than being left behind.
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, shielding, and protection; locally the final recurrence pairs restraint with enacted excellence

topics.headline: guarding at the summit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final ethical height still includes self-guarding; excellence is guarded, not unbounded.
topics.reason: The third Form VIII perfect has the same subject and form as the earlier occurrences, while its Stage 3 partner changes to aḥsanū.

words.gloss_range: final conjunction joining self-guarding to the new excellence verb
words.prose: {{ar:وَّ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the final pair a composite: guarding and excellence together. The same two-member shape as Stage 2 remains, but the second member changes, so structural sameness highlights lexical transformation.

topics.headline: final transformed pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the summit is not fear without excellence or excellence without restraint, but their coordinated pair.
topics.reason: The connector ties the final repeated ittaqaw to the new aḥsanū verb; the structural comparison with Stage 2 is local and visible.

words.gloss_range: completed Form IV excellence-making, the final-stage pivot from repair and trust into enacted beauty
words.prose: {{ar:أَحْسَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:aḥsanū}}) is the lexical pivot of the final stage. Its perfect form completes the chain of human qualifications before the coda turns to present divine love. Form IV makes the subjects agents who bring excellence into being, not merely people who possess a quality, and its arrival replaces the earlier explicit belief-and-repair wording. The cited pairing with taqwā in 3:172 confirms this as a recognizable ethical summit, while the next noun turns the action into identity.
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, goodness, excellence, and doing what is beautiful; locally Form IV selects causing excellence or beauty to appear through action

topics.headline: causative iḥsān as summit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final tier transforms prior trust and repair into enacted excellence that will define the beloved class.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV perfect; the causative beauty/excellence force survives, while the local sequence limits the claim to ethical iḥsān rather than generic beauty.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the divine-love coda after the conditional chain
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) shifts the discourse from human conditions to a divine declaration. As a resumptive connector, it keeps the coda related to the sequence without making divine love a mechanical apodosis swallowed by the condition.

topics.headline: conditions to declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse turn from completed human qualifications to an independent statement of divine love.
topics.reason: QAC marks the connector as resumptive in this position, matching the CRITICAL rows about the coda standing as a related declaration.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as explicit nominative subject of the love clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) names the subject of the coda explicitly. The legal sequence does not end with an impersonal rule but with God as the named lover of the excellence-producing class. Derivational discussions around the name may add resonance, but the local function is the proper divine name as nominative subject.
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship-directedness, and debated derivational associations; locally the proper name fixes the subject of love as God

topics.headline: God named as lover
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruling closes as a direct named divine relation rather than an abstract legal clearance.
topics.reason: The word is the explicit nominative subject of yuḥibbu; broader root disputes are kept subordinate to the local proper-name function.

topics.headline: laysa comparison belongs elsewhere
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The comparison concerns the ayah-opening negation construction, not this local word as the coda subject.
topics.reason: The row compares 5:93 with 5:116 through the laysa denial formula, but that payoff belongs to word 1 rather than to the local divine-name word.

words.gloss_range: imperfect Form IV love verb, ongoing divine affinity after completed human conditions
words.prose: {{ar:يُحِبُّ}} ({{tr:yuḥibbu}}) changes the time-feel of the ayah: completed human conditions meet ongoing divine love. The root’s love field is local, while the supplied seed and heart-core imagery gives the coda inner, generative pressure. Its formulaic recurrence with the excellence class in 5:13, 2:195, and 3:134 makes the ending more than permission; it is positive divine affinity.
words.root_gloss_range: love, affection, seed or grain, and heart-core; locally the verb selects active divine love while seed/core imagery remains secondary pressure

topics.headline: present love as closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on continuing love, not merely on the absence of blame.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an imperfect active verb with God as subject; root imagery and formulaic parallels (5:13; 2:195; 3:134) are retained as supports while the local sense remains divine love.

words.gloss_range: definite plural active participle naming the beloved class as durable makers of excellence
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ}} ({{tr:al-muḥsinīna}}) is the final object of divine love and the final identity named by the ayah. The preceding excellence-action has become a definite plural person-type: those who produce excellence. The opening believers are thus carried toward a closing identity of durable excellence, and the final sound gives that identity the ayah’s settled landing.
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, goodness, and excellence; locally the active participle turns the earlier excellence-action into identity

topics.headline: action becomes beloved identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends not with believers or the guarded, but with a durable class of excellence-makers loved by God.
topics.reason: QAC parses the word as a definite plural active participle and object of yuḥibbu; the local ḥ-s-n echo from aḥsanū supports the action-to-identity payoff.
